5.  **Upsampling (Speed-up):** If the target teacher feature dimension $M$ (e.g., 512 for LSeg) is larger than the initialized Gaussian feature dimension $N$ ($N \ll M$), apply a lightweight $1 \times 1$ convolutional decoder to upsample $F_s(\hat{I})$ from $H \times W \times N$ to $H \times W \times M$ [S1].

The claim is fully supported by the evidence in Source [S1]. Specifically, the last paragraph of Source [S1] states: 'To address this issue, we introduce a speed-up module at the end of the rasterization process. This module consists of a lightweight convolutional decoder that upsamples the feature channels with kernel size 1×1. Consequently, it is feasible to initialize f ∈ RN on 3D Gaussians with any arbitrary N ≪ M and to use this learnable decoder to match the feature channels.' This directly confirms the claim that if the target dimension M is larger than the initialized dimension N (where N << M), a lightweight 1x1 convolutional decoder is used to upsample the features from N to M.
